transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix socket or WebSocket (?token=...). Standard ACP methods pass through to the session's agent; _acpmux/* methods are the multiplexer's own.

acpNotes.session/prompt: params._meta.acpmux {promptId?: string, steer?: boolean}. The response stays at the end of the turn and gains _meta.acpmux {promptId, turnId, turnSeq} next to the agent's own _meta. The prompting connection gets _acpmux/prompt_accepted as soon as the prompt is recorded.
acpNotes.session/cancel: A notification, as ACP defines it. Sent as a request (with an id) it is answered with {} once the cancel reaches the agent, also when no turn runs.
acpNotes.session/update: Live agent updates arrive with sessionId set to the acpmux id and _meta.acpmux {seq, at, kind} merged into the agent's own _meta (the agent's keys are kept). session/load replays add replay: true.

result.listen: string|null (the bound dashboard/WebSocket address; the real port when started with --listen 127.0.0.1:0)
result.ready: boolean (false while the daemon imports the login environment and checks launchers; session/new and agent spawns wait for it)

_acpmux/reload_config.result: {reloaded: true, harnesses: string[], defaultHarness: string|null, retainedProfiles: string[], modelProbePending: true}; replaces catalog config without stopping sessions

_acpmux/defaults.result: {families: {family: {kind, profile, error, profiles, model, effort, policy, prefer, env}}, defaults} or one entry
_acpmux/defaults.note: session/new takes _meta.acpmux.harness (a family or profile: the head of -m HEAD/MODEL), .preset, .model, .effort, .policy, .name. Explicit values win over the preset, which wins over profile then family defaults.

params.name: string?
params.set: {harness (family or profile), model?, effort?, policy?, env?, description?}? (null field clears it)

_acpmux/presets.result: {presets: [{name, harness, profile, error, model, effort, policy, env, description}]} or one preset

methods._acpmux/models_note: params {refresh?: boolean} forgets reported catalogs and probes every ACP harness again before answering

params.limit: number? default 2000 (counts only records that pass kinds)
params.eventStream: boolean? (live records of this session arrive only as _acpmux/event, filtered by kinds; no session/update)

result.hasMore: boolean (older matching records exist; with afterSeq alone: newer ones)

_acpmux/attach.note: Subscribes this connection to the session's events and counts it as attached (clears unread). Without afterSeq the page is the newest `limit` records. Attaching again replaces this connection's eventStream and kinds for the session.

_acpmux/watch.note: Receive _acpmux/session_changed for every session and _acpmux/permission_pending (via: "watch") for local sessions this connection is not attached to.

params.beforeSeq: number? (page backwards: the newest `limit` matching records before it)
params.limit: number? default 5000 (counts only records that pass kinds)

result.hasMore: boolean (backwards: older matching records exist; forwards: newer ones below beforeSeq)

errors.cursor_future: afterSeq is beyond the last event

params.sessions: string[]? (empty = every running or waiting session on every host)

result.sessions: SessionSummary[] with resolved: boolean and matched: string[]

params.rules: {autoApprove?: string[], autoDeny?: string[], ask?: string[], default?: 'approve'|'deny'|'ask'} | null

_acpmux/event.note: Every mux record of an attached session. With attach eventStream: every record that passes kinds, agent session/update notifications included (the original notification in msg, its sessionId the agent's own).

params.kind: string (the record kind, or queue for queued/dequeued, permission_resolved for permission_auto, purged)

_acpmux/session_changed.note: For watchers: status, queue, permission, turn and policy changes, and peer sessions that appear, change or leave.

_acpmux/permission_pending.note: To attached connections, and to watchers that are not attached (via: watch). Remote sessions reach watchers only through session_changed.

params.promptId: string (the client's _meta.acpmux.promptId, or one acpmux generated)

_acpmux/prompt_accepted.note: Sent only to the connection that sent session/prompt, as soon as the daemon records the prompt (the queued or user_message record). Not relayed for sessions on a peer.

SessionDefaults.prefer: string[]? (profiles to use for a family, in order; first installed wins)

HarnessProfile.argv: string[] (${model} = the requested model at spawn)
HarnessProfile.models: (string | {id, name})[] declared catalog, shown ahead of the reported one
HarnessProfile.fallback: string? (profile to move to on limit or auth errors)

SessionSummary.name: string
SessionSummary.stateSeq: number (bumps on status, permission and turn changes)
SessionSummary.unread: boolean (a turn ended while no client was attached)
SessionSummary.queue: [{promptId, turnId, client, prompt, queuedAt}] prompts waiting for the running turn
SessionSummary.turn: {startedAt, client, prompt, turnId, promptId, turnSeq} | null (the running turn)

types.SessionDetail: SessionSummary plus modes, configOptions, models, agentInfo, agentCapabilities, usage, pending: [{permissionId, request}], rulesJson

Event.kind: string (method, sessionUpdate value, or mux kind)

turn_result.errorText: string? (why the turn failed, or a terminal error the harness reported in-band while the turn still completed)
turn_result.errorChunkSeqs: number[]? (the trailing agent_message_chunk records whose text is exactly errorText: hide them, show the error)
turn_result.detail: string? (outcome_unknown when the daemon restarted mid-turn)

types.EventKinds: string[]: each entry is a category or an exact record kind; a record passes when any entry matches. Categories: transcript (agent session/update except .replay, usage_update, available_commands_update, current_mode_update, config_option_update; plus mux user_message, queued, dequeued, turn_started, turn_result, permission_request, permission_auto, permission_decision, message_superseded, failover, forked, imported, mode, model, stopped, exited), mux (every mux record), wire (in/out requests, responses, harness lines and .replay records), all.

turn_started.note: turnSeq of the turn is this record's seq

turn_end.note: legacy pair of turn_result; turn_error likewise carries {error, code, turnId, turnSeq}

message_superseded.note: Recorded before the first chunk of the redelivered message. Drop the chunks of oldMessageId. Only Codex signals this (session_info_update _meta.codex.error.willRetry while a message streams); other harnesses give no signal.

daemon.readiness: acpmux daemon run binds the socket and --listen address before importing the login shell environment or checking launchers. --ready-fd N writes one line {ready: true, pid, socket, listen, webUrl} to descriptor N and closes it; the log also gets "acpmux ready {...}". _acpmux/status answers at once and reports ready and loginEnv.
daemon.shutdown: SIGTERM, SIGINT and _acpmux/shutdown remove the socket, stop every agent at once (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL after 300 ms), save sessions, sync the store and exit, within 5 s.

exitCodes.5: every permission in the turn was denied
